LESSON: PAINTING AND COLLAGE

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Creating and Executing
Topic 1.2: Painting and Collage

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Painting and Collage. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is mounting of pictures important?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. classify colour categories on the colour wheel for familiarity
2. create a collage composition to apply the characteristics
3. appreciate painting and collage techniques

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: PAINTING AND COLLAGE
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Painting and Collage helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: PAINTING AND COLLAGE
Study Painting and Collage like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Classify colour categories on the colour wheel for familiarity

What this means
In this part you learn to classify colour categories on the colour wheel for familiarity. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: classify colour categories on the colour wheel for familiarity.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Painting and Collage” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can classify colour categories on the colour wheel for familiarity. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Create a collage composition to apply the characteristics

What this means
In this part you learn to create a collage composition to apply the characteristics. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create a collage composition to apply the characteristics.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Painting and Collage in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create a collage composition to apply the characteristics. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate painting and collage techniques

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate painting and collage techniques. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate painting and collage techniques.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate painting and collage techniques. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Painting and Collage is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Painting and Collage” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: classify colour categories on the colour wheel for familiarity)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Painting and Collage in your own words. (skill: create a collage composition to apply the characteristics)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: appreciate painting and collage techniques)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Painting and Collage to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: classify colour categories on the colour wheel for familiarity.
3. Practise this skill: create a collage composition to apply the characteristics.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate painting and collage techniques.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Painting and Collage from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Painting and Collage: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Painting and Collage?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is mounting of pictures important?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Painting and Collage means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: classify colour categories on the colour wheel for familiarity.
5. Be able to: create a collage composition to apply the characteristics.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
